title: Features, preprocessing & leakage
summary: Turn raw observations into model inputs without contaminating evaluation.
html:
Turn raw observations into model inputs without contaminating evaluation.

How the pieces connect

Fit transforms only on training data

Imputers, scalers, vocabularies, target encoders, and feature selectors can learn information from data. Fit them within each training split, then apply them to validation data. A pipeline keeps preprocessing coupled to model fitting so cross-validation repeats the correct sequence.

Represent missing and categorical values

Missingness can be informative, accidental, or structurally required. Choose imputation based on the measurement process, and optionally retain a missingness indicator. One-hot encoding works for modest cardinality. Target encoding needs careful cross-fitting to avoid injecting labels into inputs.

Respect time and grouping

For forecasting, train on the past and validate on later periods. For patient records, sessions, or devices, group related rows so they do not leak across folds. Temporal joins need point-in-time correctness: the feature store must return what was available at the prediction timestamp.

Keep training and serving consistent

Package the same preprocessing for inference. Validate feature names, order, dtypes, and units at the boundary. Log aggregate input statistics and monitor drift. A model trained with meters will behave badly on centimeters even though both are valid floating-point numbers.

Worked example

from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
model = make_pipeline(
    SimpleImputer(strategy="median"),
    StandardScaler(),
    LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000),
)
# Fit only on training data; evaluate on a held-out split.

What goes wrong

Calling fit_transform on the full dataset before cross-validation leaks distribution information into every fold. A pipeline prevents this only if the split design is also correct.

Check your understanding

Should validation labels influence a feature selector?

Reveal the explanation

No. Feature selection is part of training and must be fit inside the training fold.

An operating model for features, preprocessing & leakage

Preprocessing is part of the model. A median imputer, category vocabulary, target encoder, and feature selector all encode information learned from data. Fitting them before a split lets validation influence training even if the final estimator never sees validation labels.

The gotcha. A clean workflow diagram describes dependency order. It does not prove that any boundary is correct; each transition needs its own observable acceptance test.

Worked system: one transformation, two very different outcomes

Suppose income has missing values. Filling them with the median seems harmless, but the median is learned from data. If it is calculated on the full dataset before the split, validation rows influence the training representation. The same issue appears with scaling, category vocabularies, feature selection, target encoding, and dimensionality reduction. A pipeline only protects you when its fitting step is restricted to the training fold.

The operational version matters as much as evaluation. At serving time, the pipeline must accept an unseen category, a missing field, a reordered payload, and the units supplied by the real producer. Version the feature definitions with the model, then test a raw production-shaped record through the exact same object used during training.

Notebook: Make the split an explicit artifact

Build one object that owns preprocessing and prediction. Test it on a record with reordered fields, unseen categories, missing values, and the units used by the real producer.

train_ids = set(train["record_id"])
assert not train_ids & set(test["record_id"])
assert train["event_time"].max() <= cutoff
# Fit transformations only after this boundary exists.
What to test next. 1. Split first: Create time-aware or group-aware evaluation partitions. 2. Fit on train: Learn imputers, vocabularies, and scalers only there. 3. Transform: Apply identical frozen logic to later data. 4. Serve: Validate features and monitor changed distributions.

The gotcha. A small inspection script proves only the quantities it prints. Preserve units, shapes, versions, and the input fixture beside its output.

A rigorous way to practice

  1. Split first. Create time-aware or group-aware evaluation partitions.
  2. Fit on train. Learn imputers, vocabularies, and scalers only there.
  3. Transform. Apply identical frozen logic to later data.
  4. Serve. Validate features and monitor changed distributions.

Build one object that owns preprocessing and prediction. Test it on a record with reordered fields, unseen categories, missing values, and the units used by the real producer.

Verification questions for features, preprocessing & leakage

BoundaryQuestionEvidence
Split firstWhat would show that this boundary failed?Create time-aware or group-aware evaluation partitions.
Fit on trainWhat would show that this boundary failed?Learn imputers, vocabularies, and scalers only there.
TransformWhat would show that this boundary failed?Apply identical frozen logic to later data.
ServeWhat would show that this boundary failed?Validate features and monitor changed distributions.

The gotcha. Passing each component check separately does not prove the composed path preserves identity, units, ordering, or authority.

Training-serving skew is a contract failure

A feature has a definition, timestamp, entity key, unit, missing-value rule, and availability boundary. Training and serving must implement the same contract.

  • Fit transformations on training data. Scalers, imputers, vocabularies, encoders, selectors, and learned embeddings otherwise leak evaluation information.
  • Join as of prediction time. A correct entity join can still leak a future outcome through a later snapshot.
  • Unknown categories need explicit behavior. Rejecting, mapping to an unknown token, and hashing create different failure modes.
  • Validate semantics beside schema. A numeric field can pass type checks while changing from seconds to milliseconds.

The gotcha. Reusing feature code does not guarantee reuse of source snapshots, lookup state, or execution order.
